gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the QIDI Max4 heats its 390 × 390 × 340 mm chamber with its own 500 W PTC heater, rated separately from its 700 W bed (150 W + 500 W + 700 W = 1,350 W total, with a 110 V model), while the Prusa CORE One L reaches its 60 °C chamber with no separate heater, only two fans under the heatbed pushing bed heat around the chamber.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us 'Large enclosed 3D printers' (cited, updated 2026-10-30) and 'Chamber temperature specs' (cited). Both already sort printers into active and passive chambers, give the 65 °C and 60 °C maximums, and say the CORE One L+ gets its heat from fans pushing air across the heated bed. The specs page also names a 'PTC chamber heater' for the QIDI Max4 and Plus5 in its source list. Neither page gives heater wattage, total rated power or voltage for any printer, and neither says how many watts of heater the largest chamber gets. The new part is the heater wattage. The active-versus-passive point itself is already covered.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's 'best for maximum size' pick of the QIDI Max4 for ABS, ASA and nylon. It has the largest chamber in the list (about 51.7 L) and QIDI's spec sheet gives it a dedicated 500 W chamber heater on top of the bed. The Prusa CORE One L/L+ heats its chamber only from the bed, so it is the weakest of the five for large engineering-material parts. Its own spec table lists ABS and ASA only 'with Advanced Filtration'. For the Bambu H2S and Creality K2 Plus I could not open a maker page that gives chamber heater wattage, so I can't rank all five by heater power.
